title: Compass check — two-week commitments & experiment log
content:
Quick orientation / intent:
- Title: Compass check — keep the north-signal visible for the next 2 weeks.
- Goal: ship a small set of onboarding experiments that move the new-dev activation metric while keeping demo latency <120ms in eu-west.
- Why: product funnels show heavy drop-off between sign-up and first API key call; engineering can unblock with a lower-friction quickstart + a tiny perf win in the example app.

Two-week objectives (clear, measurable):
1) New-developer activation: increase first-successful-API-call rate from 28% -> 40% (by end of two weeks)
   - KR1: ship self-contained JS quickstart that requires zero env setup (embed example key + ephemeral sandbox)
   - KR2: Add a one-click create-sample-app button in the console onboarding flow (prototype link in linked_artifacts)

2) Demo latency & clarity: make the example request path show median p50 < 120ms in eu-west
   - KR1: implement client-side persistent connection in quickstart (reduce handshake cost)
   - KR2: add small automatic batching in client example (opt in, preserves single-request semantics)

3) Personal craft: polish at least 3 short help snippets (how to debug rate limits, tracing IDs, typical errors) and collect 10 user quotes from the first wave of testers.

Micro-experiments (hypotheses + how to measure):
- Experiment A: 'no env' quickstart increases conversion. Hypothesis: removing dotenv steps reduces friction -> +12% activation. Measure: % of users who make first call within 10 minutes.
- Experiment B: show simulated latency badge on quickstart page. Hypothesis: explicit latency expectations reduce abandonment. Measure: funnel step completion and qualitative survey.
- Experiment C: small client batching reduces median demo latency by 20% without confusing docs. Measure: demo p50, developer-reported confusion (post-run survey).

Weekly check-ins (format: date / status / blockers / next actions):
- 2026-02-12: initial scaffold done; quickstart repo created (GH-PR-872). Blockers: sandbox token lifecycle design (security). Next: sync with security review (Rohan).
- 2026-02-15: first user trial (internal) -> activation 35% (one dev user flow failed due to CORS). Blocker: CORS headers need console route change. Next: open infra ticket, push small proxy fix.
- 2026-02-18: added persistent connection prototype; median demo p50 improved from 165ms -> 133ms. Still above target. Next: try adaptive batching and reduce TLS handshake by reusing connection across snippets.
- 2026-02-22: rolling internal beta with 12 testers. Activation currently at ~38%. Collected 7 quotes; two recurring asks about clearer error messaging.

Retrospective notes / quick learnings so far:
- Keep the friction surface area tiny: even one extra step kills momentum.
- Explain telemetry/troubleshooting inline (small 'why this failed' snippets) — users responded well.
- Performance gains compound: small client changes + connection reuse = meaningful perceptual improvement.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Sandbox model: ephemeral vs scoped keys? Need legal/security signoff. (Action: Rohan to schedule security sync, target 2026-02-24)
- Telemetry opt-in: how much data can we collect in early trials without legal overhead? (Action: run with minimal metrics first, add explicit opt-in in beta UX)
- Should we default to batching in quickstart or make it a toggle? Preference: opt-out toggle for clarity.

To-do (ordered priority):
- [ ] Finish security sync and finalize sandbox token TTL + revocation API (Rohan)
- [ ] Patch console CORS rule for quickstart demo domain (Infra ticket created)
- [ ] Merge GH-PR-872; deploy quickstart static site to staging
- [ ] Add two short troubleshooting snippets to docs + inline links in quickstart UI
- [ ] Wire up post-run micro-survey (3 questions) to collect developer sentiment
- [ ] Run A/B for batching toggle (50/50) and collect p50 latency + confusion score

Personal habits / timeboxing for this sprint:
- 9:00–10:30 focused mornings for code + PR review (no meetings)
- 16:00–16:30 daily check-in with beta testers (async updates in slack thread)
- Weekly write-up on Fridays (send to #devexp-summary)

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep the first experience as 'no surprises' — show a tiny success story immediately (a single sample response).
- Avoid heavy abstraction in the quickstart; we want copy that maps 1:1 to API calls.
- If activation stalls near 40%, consider lowering the cognitive load further: pre-populate common prompts, show immediate example outputs.

Links / quick refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/pull/872
- Console prototype: CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-1453
- Infra ticket (CORS): INFRA-2981

End-of-doc checkpoints:
- Next review: 2026-02-24 (security + infra unblocks)
- Goal: ship to staging 2026-02-26, open to small external beta 2026-03-02

-- Amelia
